s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic oral ulceration with granulomatous inflammation
salient_findings: Ulcer with clean base and irregular, elevated margins
Histopathological findings of dense diffuse infiltrate with lymphocytes, histiocytes, and giant cells
key_facts: 40-year-old man from eastern India
Presented with a nonhealing ulcer on the tongue for 4 months
Lesion started as a small painless mass on the right lateral aspect of the tongue
No history of trauma or tongue bite preceding the lesion
Patient denied consuming tobacco or alcohol regularly
Medical history of well-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus for 2 years
Single well-defined ulcer measuring 2 × 2 cm on the right lateral aspect of tongue
Ulcer has a clean base and irregular, elevated margins
Histopathological examination showed dense diffuse infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and giant cells
Intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo were found in histiocytes and giant cells
Special stains highlighted fungal forms
Fungal culture on Sabouraud dextrose agar was negative
HIV-1 and HIV-2 serologic testing were negative

shortlist.label: Oral histoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo found in histiocytes and giant cells, consistent with histoplasmosis

shortlist.label: Oral paracoccidioidomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of intracellular yeasts and granulomatous inflammation, which can be seen in paracoccidioidomycosis

shortlist.label: Oral blastomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Ulcer with granulomatous inflammation and presence of intracellular yeasts, which can be seen in blastomycosis

shortlist.label: Oral cryptococcosis
shortlist.why_kept: Intracellular yeasts found in histiocytes and giant cells, which can be seen in cryptococcosis, although less likely given the negative fungal culture

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation with giant cells and histiocytes, which can be seen in sarcoidosis, although less likely given the presence of intracellular yeasts

raw.rationale: The presence of intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo in histiocytes and giant cells, as seen in the histopathological examination, is characteristic of histoplasmosis. The patient's geographical location in eastern India, where histoplasmosis is more common, and the clinical presentation of a nonhealing ulcer on the tongue, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Oral paracoccidioidomycosis
rejected.why: Paracoccidioidomycosis typically presents with a more severe and disseminated disease, and the patient's clinical presentation does not match this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Oral blastomycosis
rejected.why: Blastomycosis typically presents with a more acute and severe disease, and the patient's clinical presentation does not match this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Oral cryptococcosis
rejected.why: Cryptococcosis is more commonly associated with immunocompromised patients, and the patient's HIV testing was negative, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Sarcoidosis typically presents with a more systemic disease, and the patient's clinical presentation and histopathological examination do not support this diagnosis.
